# 1. ServiceAccount для вашего входа\nku:
# 1. A ServiceAccount for your sign-in
kubectl create serviceaccount me -n vinaire

# 2. Look only (reader) — OR work fully (viewer)
kubectl create clusterrolebinding me-vinaire-reader \
  --clusterrole=vinaire-reader --serviceaccount=vinaire:me
kubectl create clusterrolebinding me-vinaire-viewer \
  --clusterrole=vinaire-viewer --serviceaccount=vinaire:me

# 3. Install apps from the Marketplace (optional)
kubectl create clusterrolebinding me-vinaire-installer \
  --clusterrole=vinaire-installer --serviceaccount=vinaire:me

# 4. Node maintenance — cordon, drain, labels, taints (optional)
kubectl create clusterrolebinding me-vinaire-node-admin \
  --clusterrole=vinaire-node-admin --serviceaccount=vinaire:me

# 5. Backups and version upgrades of what was installed from an image (optional)
kubectl create clusterrolebinding me-vinaire-lifecycle-admin \
  --clusterrole=vinaire-lifecycle-admin --serviceaccount=vinaire:me

# 5b. Vinaire's own settings — clusters, GitOps (optional)
kubectl create clusterrolebinding me-vinaire-admin \
  --clusterrole=vinaire-admin --serviceaccount=vinaire:me

# 6. A token for the sign-in screen (with a limited lifetime)
kubectl create token me -n vinaire --duration=1h

Страница входа Keycloak может выглядеть: Keycloak's sign-in page can look like Vinaire's: the wizard has the checkbox "Show Keycloak's sign-in page in Vinaire's look". The theme must be in Keycloak itself: one installed by Vinaire now already has it; in a Keycloak in this cluster that was installed earlier the button "Add the theme to this Keycloak" adds it (one restart); for a Keycloak outside the cluster download the theme there (a zip or a ConfigMap). Then run the setup again — it switches the realm to the theme. Until the theme is there the sign-in page shows only the name "Vinaire"; everything else is Keycloak's own look.
